title: What Are Hard Skills?
description: Hard skills are specific, teachable abilities or knowledge sets that are easily measurable. Examples include proficiency in a foreign language, coding in Java, accounting, or operating heavy machinery.
question: Which of the following is considered a hard skill?
explanation: Option B is correct. SQL is a specific, technical skill that can be measured and tested, making it a hard skill.

title: Quantify Your Hard Skills
description: When describing your hard skills on a resume or in an interview, be specific. Instead of saying 'I know Excel', say 'I am highly proficient in Excel, specifically in writing complex macros and VLOOKUPs'.
question: Which is the best way to describe a hard skill?

options.text: I am good at using design software.
I have 4 years of professional experience using Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator to create marketing materials.
I can use computers very well.

explanation: Option B is correct. It quantifies the experience, names the specific tools, and explains how they were applied.

title: Provide Proof
description: Hard skills are best supported by evidence. Mention any relevant certifications, degrees, portfolios, or technical tests you have passed to validate your proficiency.
question: How can you prove you have a specific hard skill?

options.text: Just promise the interviewer that you are really good at it.
Reference a recognized certification you earned or share a link to your portfolio.
Tell them your mom thinks you're very smart.

explanation: Option B is correct. Certifications and portfolios provide objective evidence of your capabilities.

title: Be Honest About Your Level
description: Never lie or exaggerate about a technical skill. If you are tested on it and fail, it ruins your credibility. It is better to admit you are a beginner but eager to learn.
question: What should you do if asked about a software tool you only used once?

options.text: Say you are an expert and hope they don't test you.
Admit you have basic familiarity but express a strong willingness and ability to learn it quickly.
Pretend you didn't hear the question.

explanation: Option B is correct. Honesty builds trust, and showing a willingness to learn turns a weakness into a display of a positive attitude.

title: Continuous Learning
description: Technology and methodologies change rapidly. Showing that you actively keep your hard skills updated through courses, reading, or personal projects is highly attractive to employers.
question: Why is it important to keep learning new hard skills?

options.text: Because industries evolve and keeping your skills sharp ensures you remain competitive and valuable.
So you can brag about it to your friends.
It isn't. Once you learn something, you never need to update it.

explanation: Option A is correct. Continuous learning shows you are proactive and adaptable to industry changes.
